podcast.body: Released in 2004 after a long period of silence and extensive touring, this album was primarily made by Liam Howlett alone. It received very mixed and polarizing reviews from fans and critics, with opinions ranging from enthusiastic approval to strong dislike. It was considered a controversial album for many Prodigy fans. The album represented a "sad but necessary evolution," as the hardcore techno culture in which The Prodigy originated had died out, and electronic music had moved in very different directions by the new millennium. Despite the initial controversy, the album's sound is considered "really current" even today, as recreating an album like "The Fat of the Land" in 2004 would not have made sense in the changed musical landscape. "It was a rather controversial album for Prodigy fans."
